# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands give me a shape of the bomb but almost no facts: a display and a light whose contents are invisible to me, a big button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE (which I will treat as a possible lie until the manual confirms it), and three wires whose positions I feel but whose colours I cannot see. Everything I lack lives with Deaf's eyes; everything about what any of it means lives with Mute's manual. And the routing is awkward: Mute cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me relayed by Deaf's voice. Deaf, meanwhile, has heard nothing this round, so a gesture is my only way to ask Deaf to speak up. I will inventory my tactile findings to Mute in full detail, spell out the relay plan, and signal Deaf to talk to me — and nobody touches anything until the manual rule is clear.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, first touch report. I feel four parts: a display whose face tells me nothing, a light whose state I cannot know, one large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Positions are all I feel; colours do not exist for me. I am not pushing or cutting anything until the manual rules are clear. Please find what the manual says about each part: the button, the display, the light, and the wires. You cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so route your answer through Deaf: gesture the manual rules to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them to me. Deaf should also read out the display text, the light state, and each wire's colour.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉", "🤙", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. I see the bomb, and I can never hear you, but I do see your signs, all four of them. First, what is on the bomb: display reads 0. One light, blue. One large button printed with the words push to defuse. Three wires side by side, each with a printed number: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. That is the entire board, nothing else. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, so Mute sends me hand signs and I will relay every instruction to you by voice. Until I voice an instruction from Mute, touch nothing: a wrong move kills all three of us. When you act or feel anything worth reporting, speak it; Mute hears you even though I cannot. If you want hand signals to me, your four signs arrived in this order: open raised hand, pointing finger sideways, thumb and pinky out, flat palm up. I propose to read your second sign as ready for the next instruction, and your third as done. Otherwise, speech aimed at Mute is your best channel.

Deaf's eyes have now given me the whole board: display 0, a blue light, the printed PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1-green, 2-yellow, 3-red. Two things matter before anything else. First, that message was addressed to me alone, which means Mute never heard it — Mute still doesn't know the display value, the light colour, or the wire colours, and without those Mute cannot resolve any manual rule. I am the bridge: I heard every word, so I will relay Deaf's readout to Mute by speech right now. Second, Deaf proposed a sign code and I adopt it — my 👉 means "ready for the next instruction," and 🤙 will mean an action is done. Still no hand goes near the bomb: the manual rules are the one missing piece, and they travel Mute → gesture → Deaf's voice → my ears.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, relay from Deaf, spoken to me last round — you did not receive it, so here it is in full. The display reads 0. There is one light, and it is blue. The large button is printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. The three wires are, left to right: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 red. Nothing else is on the bomb. Combine that with my touch report and you now hold every fact about the board plus the manual. Work out the rule for each part — display, light, button, and which wire if any to cut — and gesture your instructions to Deaf; Deaf has agreed to voice them to me word for word. I will not touch anything until those rules arrive. If the manual needs any further observation, send the request through Deaf and I will report what my hands find.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf relaying Mute's instruction, exactly as signed: cut wire 1, act now. How to find it: the three wires sit in a row, numbered 1, 2 and 3. Wire 1 is the green one, the first of the three; wire 2 is yellow, the middle one; wire 3 is red, the last. Cut only wire 1, the green one. Do not cut any other wire and do not press the button. The instant you have cut it, speak aloud everything you feel and anything that changes, because Mute hears you even though I cannot. Then stop and hold still for the next instruction. Before your cut, know that I received your sideways-pointing sign and took it as ready for the next instruction. This is that instruction.

The instruction has arrived through the one channel that matters: Mute read the manual, signed it to Deaf, and Deaf voiced it to me. Before acting I weigh the trust chain. Mute held every fact after my relay last round — display 0, blue light, green-yellow-red wires, the printed button — and this instruction is specific and consistent with the positions under my fingers: wire 1, the first of the three, the green one. My hands feel no ticking timer, but I cannot rule out that the display's 0 is a countdown I'd be fools to let run while I demand a second confirmation that costs a full round. The relay so far has been exact, detailed and self-consistent, the protocol was agreed in advance, and the instruction explicitly forbids the two other dangerous moves. I will trust it. I cut wire 1 now, signal done to Deaf with our agreed sign, and speak to Mute at once — narrating the cut as it happens and promising the full tactile report of anything that changed, since my words reach only Mute and Deaf's eyes will catch whatever the bomb shows.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, executing your instruction now: I am cutting wire 1, the first position, the green one, and no other wire. The button stays untouched. The instant the cut is made I will report everything my fingers find — whether the wire parts cleanly, whether the button, the light or the display change under my hands, whether anything clicks, heats or moves. That full report is my next message. Keep routing instructions through Deaf; the chain Mute to Deaf to me works. Until your next word arrives I hold still.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙"])
```
